section_summary: This section (pages 363–419) of Record Group 59, decimal file 894.032 documents the political and legislative aftermath of the February 20, 1936 Japanese general election and the February 26 military insurrection, focusing on the 69th extraordinary session of the Imperial Diet convened in May 1936. It consists of diplomatic despatches, telegrams, and State Department memoranda detailing parliamentary interpellations, policy addresses by Premier Koki Hirota and Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita, and sharp attacks by Diet members on military extremism and army indiscipline. The records also provide analyses and digests of forty-five economic, financial, and national defense measures enacted during the session, as well as consular reporting on Chinese and Japanese reactions to Japan's foreign policy pronouncements.

subfiles.about: Concludes a periodic Embassy report discussing Japanese financial trends for December and a judicial inquiry into the Omotokyo sect.
subfiles.summary: Periodic report page: December financial trends, steel market and stock peaks, and the Kyoto court's probe of the Omotokyo sect.
subfiles.title: Section of Periodic Report on Japan: Financial Trends and Miscellaneous Activities

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 1706 regarding the February 20, 1936 Diet election and the February 26 coup d'état.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 1706 (March 5, 1936): the February 20 election and its bearing on the February 26 coup attempt.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 1706

subfiles.about: Analyzes the February 20, 1936 Diet election results and their direct connection to the February 26 military uprising.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the Japanese general election of February 20, 1936, where the Minseito achieved substantial gains while the Seiyukai lost its majority, and the proletarian Shakai Taishuto increased its seats. The despatch reviews campaign platforms, the military's demand for a stronger cabinet, and public reactions to the election outcome. Grew concludes that the uprising of February 26 by radical young army officers was precipitated largely by despair over the Minseito's victory and the survival of the moderate Okada Cabinet, while noting that several of the military's state-socialist objectives coincided closely with the platform of the Shakai Taishuto.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1706: The Diet Election of February 20, 1936, and Its Bearing on the Uprising of February 26, 1936

subfiles.about: Reports opening policy addresses delivered before the Diet by Premier Hirota and the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and War.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Hirota's opening addresses to the 69th Diet, including constitutional government, defense, China and USSR, and War Minister Terauchi's blaming the February 26 incident on radical elements.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 95 from Tokyo: Opening Addresses to the 69th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Official English text of Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita's foreign policy address delivered before the extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Minister Hachiro Arita sets forth Japan's foreign policy principles before the Diet, emphasizing Japan's role as the stabilizing force in East Asia and its special ties with Manchukuo. He reviews Soviet-Manchukuo border negotiations, direct talks between Manchukuo and Outer Mongolia, and urges China to accept the three principles formulated by Premier Hirota. Arita also expresses hopes for continued friendship with Great Britain and the United States, while warning against international trade barriers, foreign economic blocs, and the spread of communist influence.
subfiles.title: Text of Foreign Minister Arita's Speech Before the Diet, May 6, 1936

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum reviewing Tokyo Despatch No. 1830 on the opening proceedings and interpellations of the Diet session.
subfiles.from: W. T. T. (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 1830: the Emperor's unprecedented opening message regretting February 26, Tomita elected Speaker, and frank interpellations criticizing the Army with evasive replies.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1830

subfiles.about: Reports on the proceedings of the 69th Diet session from May 4 to May 13, including interpellations, bills, and enclosed press translations.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides a detailed report on the proceedings of the extraordinary Diet session from May 4 to May 13, 1936, including party alignments, proposed legislation such as the seditious publications and automobile industry control bills, and cabinet speeches. The report describes remarkably bold interpellations by politicians such as Takao Saito and Chokichi Miyawaki attacking army interference in politics, military responsibility for the February 26 incident, and the court-martial of Lieutenant Colonel Aizawa. Appended as enclosures are the complete English press translations from the Japan Advertiser and Japan Times of Premier Hirota's and Foreign Minister Arita's addresses.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1830: Proceedings of the Diet from May 4 to May 13, Inclusive

subfiles.about: Reports Chinese and Japanese reactions in Tsingtao to Foreign Minister Arita's Diet address on Japanese foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Consul Sokobin reports little interest at Tsingtao in Arita's May 6 Diet address; Japanese see their China policy as set, and traders are absorbed by Tientsin smuggling losses.
subfiles.title: Despatch from American Consulate, Tsingtao: Japanese Foreign Minister's Address

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum outlining Tokyo Despatch No. 1869 on the close of the 69th Diet session and legislative output.
subfiles.from: W. T. T. (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 1869: the 69th Diet showed unusual free speech and criticism of military indiscipline; 45 bills passed, the automobile control bill most important to American interests.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1869

subfiles.about: Reports on the final two weeks of the 69th Diet session, legislative debates, enacted measures, and party statements.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew details the concluding two weeks of the 69th Diet session, which was extended by two days by Imperial Ordinance before closing on May 27, 1936. The report covers debates on contentious measures including the seditious publications bill, the employee retirement allowance bill, and the defeated national mobilization secrets bill, as well as the controversy surrounding peer Jusha Tsumura's remarks criticizing military officer courage. The Diet passed forty-five bills and an expanded budget of over 2.31 billion yen reflecting army demands, while political parties issued statements demanding that the Cabinet and military deliver on promised administrative reforms and strict internal discipline.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1869: The 69th Diet Session from May 14 to Its Close on May 27

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 1829 regarding Premier Hirota's forecast of the Diet session and party representation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 1829: Hirota predicts a quiet Diet opening on May 1, 1936, with party strength figures from the Osaka Mainichi.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 1829

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing key enactments reported in Tokyo Despatch No. 1998's legislative digest.
subfiles.from: W. T. T. (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 1998: 45 laws enacted in May 1936, including extension of the Trade Protection Law, export permits for staples and an Aviation Law barring foreign commercial aircraft.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1998

subfiles.about: Transmits a detailed legal digest of the forty-five laws passed by the 69th extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits an extensive digest summarizing forty-five laws enacted during the extraordinary Diet session ending May 27, 1936. The enclosed digest details measures including the three-year extension of the Trade Protection Law, revisions to the National Tax Collection Law, authorization for national bond issues and special account transfers for the 1936-37 budget, increased loan limits for Manchurian Incident expenditures and gratuities, relief extensions for banks affected by the 1927 panic, sericultural and cocoon disposal regulations, Chinese cultural undertaking subsidies, and the charters for the Central Bank for Commercial and Industrial Cooperative Societies and the Northeastern Industrial Company.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1998: Legislation Enacted at the May 1 - May 27 Diet Session
